summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as teams deploy LLM-powered applications at scale, requiring visibility into prompts, traces, output quality, hallucinations, and spiraling API costs. New Relic reports 30% quarter-over-quarter growth in AI monitoring adoption, reflecting how critical these tools are for optimizing performance, controlling spend, and ensuring reliability. The right choice depends on your stack, budget, and preference for open-source versus managed solutions.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: Prompts, traces, LLM workflows, token usage, latency, and output quality in production, with deep native integration for LangChain-based applications.
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus tier $39 per seat/month with overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention. Trace-heavy workloads can add 5-10% of underlying LLM API spend.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain who want tightly integrated, end-to-end tracing and evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API requests, cost across 300+ models, token usage, latency, and per-user or per-department spend via a lightweight proxy/gateway.
features: Cost computation across 300+ models via model-cost repository
Fast cost governance setup (under five minutes)
tools.pricing: Free tier at 10,000 requests/month; Helicone Pro reaches the 100,000-trace milestone at around $79, making it cost-effective for high-volume deployments.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting instant, low-overhead cost visibility and governance without deep framework integration.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: Both ML training and LLM workloads via W&B Weave, tracking experiments, model performance, prompts, traces, and evaluations in a unified platform.
features: Unified ML and LLM observability (W&B Weave)
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals and small projects; team and enterprise tiers are consumption/seat-based with custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams running both traditional ML and LLM workloads that need a single platform for unified monitoring.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM and ML model performance, embeddings, RAG pipelines, output quality, drift, and evaluations, with strong OpenTelemetry-based tracing.
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize AI managed enterprise platform uses custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Multi-framework teams and those needing OpenTelemetry-native, vendor-agnostic evaluation and monitoring.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: Prompts, traces, cost tracking, online evaluations, and LLM workflows with an open-source, self-hostable core.
tools.pricing: Free open-source self-hosted option; managed cloud offers a free tier with usage-based paid plans, cost-effective for high-volume deployments.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, cost-controllable observability stack with full data ownership.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, token usage, and latency using open standards; exports telemetry to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend.
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; costs depend on the backend/observability platform you export telemetry to.
tools.best_for: Multi-framework setups wanting standards-based, portable instrumentation that plugs into existing observability infrastructure.

cost_tips: Use a gateway/proxy like Helicone to track spend across models and set per-user or per-department budgets, enabling cost governance in minutes.
Implement prompt and response caching to avoid paying for repeated identical or near-identical requests.
Route requests to cheaper or smaller models for simpler tasks, reserving premium models for complex queries (model tiering/routing).

Watch per-trace and per-span overage pricing carefully at scale, and consider self-hosting open-source tools like Langfuse or Phoenix for high-volume workloads where managed trace costs can reach 5-10% of API spend.
